text: Calms down when spoken to or picked up

text: Tries to use a spoon

text: Eats with a spoon

text: Plays next to other children and sometimes plays with them

text: Shows you what she can do by saying, “Look at me!”

text: Follows simple routines when told, like helping to pick up toys when you say, “It’s clean-up time.”

text: Says about 50 words

text: Says two or more words together, with one action word, like “Doggie run”

text: Names things in a book when you point and ask, “What is this?”

text: Says words like “I,” “me,” or “we”

text: Uses things to pretend, like feeding a block to a doll as if it were food

text: Shows simple problem-solving skills, like standing on a small stool to reach something

text: Follows two-step instructions like “Put the toy down and close the door.”

text: Shows he knows at least one color, like pointing to a red crayon when you ask, “Which one is red?”

text: Talks with you in conversation using at least two back-and-forth exchanges

text: Says what action is happening in a picture or book when asked, like “running,” “eating,” or “playing”

text: Says first name, when asked

text: Talks well enough for others to understand, most of the time

text: Draws a circle, when you show him how

text: Avoids touching hot objects, like a stove, when you warn her

text: Strings items together, like large beads or macaroni

text: Puts on some clothes by himself, like loose pants or a jacket

text: Uses a fork

text: Pretends to be something else during play (teacher, superhero, dog)

text: Avoids danger, like not jumping from tall heights at the playground

text: Likes to be a “helper”

text: Changes behavior based on where she is (place of worship, library, playground)

text: Says sentences with four or more words

text: Says some words from a song, story, or nursery rhyme”

text: Talks about at least one thing that happened during his day, like “I played soccer.”

text: Answers simple questions like “What is a coat for?” or “What is a crayon for?”

text: Names a few colors of items
source: CDC Learn the Signs. Act Early.

text: Tells what comes next in a well-known story

text: Draws a person with three or more body parts

text: Catches a large ball most of the time

text: Serves herself food or pours water, with adult supervision

text: Unbuttons some buttons

text: Holds crayon or pencil between fingers and thumb (not a fist)

text: Follows rules or takes turns when playing games with other children

text: Sings, dances, or acts for you

text: Does simple chores at home, like matching socks or clearing the table after eating

text: Answers simple questions about a book or story after you read or tell it to him

text: Keeps a conversation going with more than three back-and-forth exchanges

text: Uses or recognizes simple rhymes (bat-cat, ball-tall)

text: Names some numbers between 1 and 5 when you point to them

text: Pays attention for 5 to 10 minutes during activities. For example, during story time or making arts and crafts (screen time does not count)

text: Writes some letters in her name

text: Names some letters when you point to them

text: Buttons some buttons

text: Hops on one foot
